title: microthrottle-calibration-cheatsheet-kyoshi
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational notes and an experiment log for tuning micro-throttle and short-window backpressure settings on a 4xA100 serving pool. Personal reference — rough numbers, heuristics, and a couple of cheap plots (ASCII) to help triage transient sovling during customer demo runs.

Context / why: 
- Demo runs in us-west-2 exposed 50-200ms p99 spikes during 3–6s microbursts (small requests, high QPS).
- We suspect aggressive batching + cold KV cache + ephemeral CPU scheduling on proxy VMs.
- Need a lightweight calibration procedure for on-call and SRE to quickly set micro-throttle knobs under load.

Quick summary recommendations (short):
- Set micro_throttle.window_ms = 40 for low-latency clients (interactive chat)
- soft_backoff.alpha = 0.65 + min_cooldown_ms = 80 to avoid oscillation in 200–800rps bursts
- prefer prefill_enabled = true for routes with context < 256 tokens
- use dynamic_priority = client_latency_sensitive for 95% of demo traffic; reserve background lane for batch jobs

Experiment setup (notes):
- Fleet: 4xA100 (80GB), mixed p4 and p3 proxy VMs, runtime commit: runtime@b2f3ae4
- Workload: synthetic Zipfian small payloads (avg tokens=32), client generator with Poisson superposed with scheduled microbursts (10s quiet / 6s 500rps spike / 20s steady 150rps)
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, queue_depth, batch_size_distribution, kvcache.hit_rate, GPU_util, cpu_runq
- Traces for 30s windows captured on run start/end (x-ray traces + local perf counters)

Baseline (no micro-throttle):
- steady 150rps: p50=22ms, p95=78ms, p99=240ms
- during burst 500rps: p50=28ms, p95=220ms, p99=980ms (several timeouts logged)
- mean batch_size during burst = 18, but high variance (2–64) leading to long tail from some huge batches + CPU serialization

Run A — window_ms=20, no prefill:
- steady: p50=24ms, p95=92ms, p99=260ms
- burst: p50=30ms, p95=320ms, p99=1100ms
- observation: too-small window created more small batches and increased scheduling overhead on proxies.

Run B — window_ms=40, soft_backoff.alpha=0.5:
- steady: p50=21ms, p95=70ms, p99=220ms
- burst: p50=26ms, p95=160ms, p99=520ms
- kvcache.hit_rate improved by ~6% due to slightly larger batch prefixes; batch variance still high but less extreme.

Run C — window_ms=40, soft_backoff.alpha=0.65, min_cooldown_ms=80, prefill_enabled=true:
- steady: p50=20ms, p95=66ms, p99=200ms
- burst: p50=25ms, p95=110ms, p99=320ms
- batch_size mean ~22, variance reduced (6–36), fewer timeouts.
- GPU_util increased 7%, overall cost per token down ~4% for this workload.

Cheap ASCII visualization (p99 vs time, sampled):
- baseline: ---------------^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ (long elevated tail during bursts)
- run C: -----------^^^^^^^^^^^^ (shorter peak, faster recovery)

Heuristics derived (rules of thumb):
1) Start at window_ms = max(20, median_client_rtt/2) and increase in 10ms steps if p95/p99 are volatile.
2) Use soft_backoff.alpha ~ 0.6–0.75 for short high-amplitude bursts to dampen re-sends; lower alpha for long sustained increases.
3) min_cooldown_ms should be tuned with your retry/backoff policy — pick value that exceeds an average RPC punishing spike (experimentally we used 80–120ms).
4) Prefill gives disproportionate wins when context < 128 tokens and request rate has short contiguous spikes.
5) If batch variance > 3x mean, check proxy CPU runq and serialization hotspots; micro-throttle alone won't fix serialization bottlenecks.

Quick troubleshooting checklist (on-call):
- Are p99 spikes coincident with sudden batch_size growth? -> check batch distribution dashboard.
- kvcache.hit_rate drop? If yes, enable prefill on the route and re-run a 1-min smoke test.
- If proxy cpu_runq > 2 for >30s, reduce window_ms and/or increase proxy VM count.
- If oscillation observed after throttle change (latency flips high/low every 10–40s) -> increase min_cooldown_ms and alpha.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Test with heterogeneous model sizes: 7B vs 70B to validate knob portability.
- Explore adaptive window: measure inter-arrival variance and transiently increase window to keep batch variance bounded.
- Evaluate warm-pool + prefill interaction for multi-tenant scenarios (will prefill increase cross-tenant interference?).

Notes / micro-log entries (timestamps local):
- 2025-02-12 09:12 — baseline run reproduced on staging; saw the 980ms p99 spike.
- 2025-02-12 11:03 — run B improved tail but still inconsistent.
- 2025-02-18 16:40 — run C deployed to demo cluster; p99 during scripted demo stayed < 350ms.

Attachments / quick links:
- related perf traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/MICRO-4521 (sample)
- quick dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/ingress/microburst-calib?orgId=1

Next steps (for me):
- Turn the heuristics into an automation playbook (Confluence page + a small CLI to compute recommended knobs given sample trace).
- Pair with Priya to run heterogeneous-model sweep next week.
